_note: The kit an operator wears (src/game/gear.ts). The figures were a bare mannequin in a flat colour, which is the single biggest reason they read as a toy rather than a soldier: a shipped shooter's character is a silhouette made of a helmet, a vest, a mask and a pack, and it is that outline you recognise at 80 m, not a face. Every piece here is built from boxes and cylinders in the operator's own colours rather than downloaded, because a rigged, weighted garment is a different kind of asset from a prop and the shape is what does the work. Sizes are metres on a figure 1.8 m tall. `at` is where the piece sits on the bone it hangs from, measured in that bone’s REST pose: x its right, y up it, z in front of it. From there the piece turns with the bone, so a helmet leans when the head leans into the sights and the eyes it covers lean with it.

vest._note: a plate carrier: a front plate, a back plate and the webbing between them, on the upper spine

pack._note: a daypack high on the back, with a roll on top: the outline that says somebody is carrying something

helmet._note: a shell over the crown with a short rear lip, and a rail down each side

shades._note: one dark bar across the eyes, on its own strap. A visor reads at any distance; two lenses do not

mask._note: a gas mask: a snout over the nose and mouth, a filter can on the cheek, and the straps round the back

hood._note: a soft hood standing off the back of the head, open at the front

brim._note: a cap peak over the eyes

shoulders._note: hard plates over the deltoids, on the upper arms

pouches._note: a drop pouch on the right thigh and a holster on the left

knees._note: knee pads on the shins, just under the joint
